title: Three-dimensional Patterning of Engineered Biofilms with a Do-it-yourself Bioprinter
protocol: Remove the extruder and heater from a commercial 3D printer.
Unplug the wiring controlling the removed elements from the main circuit board.
Disable the algorithm in the printing software that delays printing until operational temperature is reached.
Connect a pipette tip via silicon tubing to a 5 mL syringe loaded into a syringe pump.
Mount the connected pipette tip onto the 3D printer extruder head as a replacement for the original extruder.
If using more than one type of bio-ink, mount additional tubing system(s) and pipette tip(s) to the printer.
Add 4 mL of 5 M CaCl2 solution to 400 mL of 1% w/v agar dissolved in LB medium supplemented with antibiotics and inducers.
Dispense 20 mL of the LB-agar solution into each 150 mm x 15 mm Petri dish.
Dry the Petri dishes for 30 minutes at room temperature with the lid half-open.
Prepare a sodium alginate solution (3% w/v).
Heat the sodium alginate solution to the boiling point three times to sterilize it.
Store the sterilized sodium alginate solution at 4°C until use.
Grow E. coli MG1655 PRO ΔcsgA ompR234 bacteria carrying plasmids pSB1C3-green fluorescent protein overnight at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm in LB medium containing chloramphenicol and rhamnose.
Centrifuge the cell culture for 5 min at 3,220 x g to pellet the bacteria.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the bacteria pellet in 10 mL of LB medium.
Add 10 mL of sodium alginate (3% w/v) to the resuspended bacteria.
Install and open the 3D printing software on a computer.
Connect the 3D printer to the computer.
Move the printhead to its home position by clicking the home button for X, Y, and Z axes.
Place a prepared printing substrate onto a particular location on the printing bed.
Calibrate the height of the printhead in the Z axis.
Raise the printhead to a height of 22 mm under manual control.
Position the printhead overtop of the plate and move it down until the pipette tip contacts the printing surface.
Assign this Z-axis position as Z1 (the height of the printing surface).
Raise the printhead.
Move it outside of the plate area manually in the X, Y, and Z axes.
Enter Z1 + Z2 into the printing program as the Z-value during printing.
Program the printing shape by a self-developed point-by-point coordinate-determined method according to the desired trajectory.
Define only the start and end points for a straight line.
Include additional points on curved lines for smoother curves.
Move the printhead manually to every point sequentially, recording coordinates in order.
Enter all recorded coordinates as well as printhead moving speed into the G-code editor.
Lift the printhead to a distance higher than the plate edge (20 mm) before printing.
Lift the printhead to a distance higher than the plate edge after printing.
Move directly out of the plate region after lifting the printhead.
Save this program as a G-code file and load it for use in subsequent prints.
Re-measure the Z axis height for each new printing substrate.
Load the liquid bio-ink into syringe(s).
Mount the syringes in the syringe pump(s) of the 3D bioprinter.
Start the syringe pump manually before the printhead comes into contact with the printing surface.
Print the bio-ink onto the printing substrate by clicking the Print button.
Control the printhead movement entirely by the software during printing.
Stop the syringe pump as soon as the printhead arrives at the last point of printing.
Control all movements of the printhead in the G-code editor.
Type in the printing height of the first layer.
Increase the Z-value in the G-code by 0.2 millimeters for the second layer to increase the printing height.
Increase the Z-value by 0.1 millimeters when moving to a higher layer.
Do not move the plate during the printing process.
Measure the width and height of the printed hydrogel using a steel ruler placed underneath or alongside the sample.
Incubate the printed samples at room temperature for 3−6 days to allow the production of biofilm components (curli fibers).
Image the plates using a camera or fluorescent scanner.
Add 20 mL of 0.5 M sodium citrate solution (pH = 7 adjusted with NaOH) to the printing substrates.
Incubate the samples for 2 h with 30 rpm shaking at room temperature.
Discard the liquid and image the plates again to compare with the images of the plates before citrate treatment.
